issues.body:
workflow_triggers was moved to cron_map.py and its failure type changed from AlarmError to CronMapError. Both subclass RuntimeError but are unrelated siblings (ci-latency-alert.py:127 `class AlarmError(RuntimeError)`, cron_map.py:27 `class CronMapError(RuntimeError)`).

The LIVE path still calls it: run() (line 2324) -> fetch_lanes() -> workflow_triggers() at line 911, with no intermediate handler. main() at line 2414 catches only AlarmError, so a workflow file that is unparseable YAML, or is not a mapping, or a runner without PyYAML, now propagates a raw traceback instead of taking the designed branch: `::error::ci-latency watchdog infrastructure failure: {exc}` and return code 2.

The diff updated exactly one call site for this rename -- the self-test at line 1349 (`except AlarmError` -> `except CronMapError`) -- and left the live handler untouched. That asymmetry is the tell: the self-test was made to pass while the production contract silently drifted.

Not fail-open (the step still errors, and groom-sweep.yml's step is `continue-on-error: true` either way), so severity is major rather than blocker. But it breaks the error taxonomy AlarmError documents as "The detector itself is broken. Never mask a choke.", and no assertion covers it.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) catch both at the entry point: `except (AlarmError, CronMapError) as exc:` at ci-latency-alert.py:2414, or (b) preferably re-establish the single taxonomy at the seam -- wrap the fetch_lanes call (or workflow_triggers at line 911) so CronMapError is re-raised as AlarmError with the offending path in the message. Then add a self-test row asserting the polarity: feed main() (or fetch_lanes) a tree containing an unparseable workflow and assert it returns the infrastructure-failure code / emits the `::error::` annotation rather than raising -- otherwise this same drift recurs on the next move.
issues.title: Live path: workflow_triggers now raises CronMapError, which main()'s `except AlarmError` no longer catches

issues.body:
The removed workflow_triggers was the only reader of `_YAML_IMPORT_ERROR` (set at line 105). After this diff the name is dead in this module.

More than cosmetic: the `yaml is None` check that turned a missing PyYAML into a named AlarmError went with it, but ci-latency-alert.py still calls `yaml.safe_load(...)` directly at line 2204 (the groom-sweep seam block). With PyYAML absent, `yaml` is None and that line now raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'safe_load'` instead of the intended fail-loud AlarmError. cron_map.py keeps its own guard, so the live lane path is still covered -- this is the self-test seam only, and groom-sweep.yml installs PyYAML in a prior step, which is why it will not bite in CI today.
issues.fix_hint: Either drop the now-dead `try/except ImportError` block and `_YAML_IMPORT_ERROR` from ci-latency-alert.py and import yaml unconditionally (letting ImportError surface at module load), or keep the guard and add an explicit `if yaml is None: raise AlarmError(f"PyYAML unavailable: {_YAML_IMPORT_ERROR}")` before the safe_load at line 2204.
issues.title: _YAML_IMPORT_ERROR is now orphaned, and the remaining yaml.safe_load lost its fail-loud guard

issues.body:
expand_field is exported and consumed by ci-latency-alert.py's expected_firings with four other bound pairs: hours (0,23), day-of-month (1,31), month (1,12) and day-of-week (0,7) -- the last relying on the unusual hi=7 plus the caller's `d % 7` fold.

Every assertion in cron_map.py's _self_test reaches expand_field only through cron_minutes, i.e. always with lo=0, hi=59. The boundary behaviour this module now OWNS for the other four ranges (notably that 7 is accepted for dow, and that dom starts at 1 rather than 0) is asserted nowhere in the owning module. That coverage currently survives only incidentally via expected_firings rows in the consumer's suite -- exactly the arrangement this PR is trying to eliminate, since a future consumer could drop those rows and leave the owner untested at those bounds.
issues.fix_hint: Add a few direct expand_field rows to cron_map.py's _self_test with hand-computed expectations, e.g. `check("dow accepts 7 as the second Sunday spelling", expand_field("7", 0, 7), {7})`, `check("dom is 1-based", raises(CronError, lambda: expand_field("0", 1, 31)), True)`, and one hour-range case such as `expand_field("22-23", 0, 23) == {22, 23}`.
issues.title: expand_field is now the owner for five field ranges but the self-test only exercises minutes (0-59)

issues.body:
_workflow_crons (line 127) wraps parse failures to append `at {path}`, which is genuinely useful when one of ~13 lanes is malformed. But the cron expansion happens later, at line 160 in schedule_minute_map, outside that wrapper: a bad cron raises CronError carrying only the expression, e.g. "value outside 0-59 in '3,60 * * * *'", with no indication of which workflow file it came from.

The fail-closed polarity is correct and is asserted ("malformed lane refuses instead of disappearing"); this is purely about the operator's ability to find the offending lane from the failure message.
issues.fix_hint: Wrap the per-expression loop in schedule_minute_map so the path is attached, e.g. `try: minutes.update(cron_minutes(expression))` / `except CronError as exc: raise CronError(f"{exc} in {WORKFLOWS_DIR}/{path.name}") from exc`. Keep the raised type CronError so the existing self-test row and the fail-closed contract are unchanged.
issues.title: schedule_minute_map annotates CronMapError with the offending path but not CronError

verdict.summary:
Extraction of cron expansion + the derived schedule map out of ci-latency-alert.py into a new standalone scripts/cron_map.py. The mechanics are mostly well executed: cron_map.py has no cross-script imports so the two importlib consumers (dispatch-tick-floor.py's _cron_minutes_module, regate-sweep.py's _cron_map_module) now exec_module a small standalone file instead of a huge one; dispatch-tick-floor's REQUIRED_FILES seam is exact-equality and matches dispatch.yml's new sparse-checkout list; groom-sweep.yml and regate-sweep.yml sparse-checkouts were updated in step with REQUIRED_FILES/CRON_MAP_SCRIPT; cron_map.py is enrolled in selftest-suite.txt; and the new --self-test is NON-VACUOUS (hand-computed expectations, refusal probes carrying both polarities so the raises() helper cannot be always-true, and a missing-tree case correctly placed outside the TemporaryDirectory). The bare `from cron_map import ...` resolves in every known invocation path (worker-live.sh runs `python3 "$root/$script"`, groom-sweep runs `python3 registry/scripts/ci-latency-alert.py`), so sys.path[0] is always the scripts dir. No fail-open path, no permissions/secret/pinning changes.

Blocking on one MAJOR: the refactor changed the exception type on a LIVE code path and updated only the self-test call site, not the live handler. workflow_triggers moved from raising AlarmError to raising CronMapError, but ci-latency-alert.py's fetch_lanes (live, reached from run()) still calls it and main() still catches ONLY AlarmError. An unparseable/non-mapping workflow YAML, or a missing PyYAML, now escapes the designed "detector is broken" handler as an uncaught traceback instead of the `::error::ci-latency watchdog infrastructure failure` annotation and rc 2. It fails loud rather than open, so this is a contract/diagnostics regression, not a trust hole — but it is an incomplete refactor of a deliberately documented error taxonomy ("Never mask a choke"), and nothing tests it.
